issues.legal_issue: A person’s status as a village officeholder or resident, without a sufficient connection to the trust, does not establish the interest required to bring a suit concerning its administration.
material_facts: The plaintiffs relied on their status as village Lambardars and residents to claim an interest in the trust.
The trust’s land had been donated by inferior owners, but there was no proof that either plaintiff owned land or was a successor-in-interest of a donor.
The institution’s free kitchen served visitors, and there was no proof that village residents were entitled as of right to receive food there.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs had no sufficient interest in the trust in their capacities as Lambardars or village residents and could not institute the suit on those grounds.
issues.legal_principle: Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires a plaintiff to have a clear interest in the particular trust, beyond the general interest shared by members of the public or a religious community. The Court applied Vaidyanatha Ayyar v. Swaminatha Ayyar, which explains that the requirement prevents interference in charitable-trust administration merely in the interests of others and without a real interest of the plaintiff.

predicates.public_trust_administration_suit: The proceeding seeks relief concerning the administration of a public trust.
predicates.lambardar_without_land_link: The claimant relies on village officeholder status but has no established ownership or succession link to land donated to the trust.
predicates.village_resident_without_food_entitlemen: The claimant relies on village residence where a kitchen serves visitors, but residents have no established right to receive food there.
predicates.claimant_lacks_sufficient_interest: The claimant does not have sufficient interest in the trust to bring the administration suit.

issues.definition: When an administration suit concerns a public trust, reliance only on village officeholder status without a land link, or village residence without an entitlement to the trust’s food service, means the claimant lacks sufficient interest to bring the suit.

issues.legal_issue: A person’s Sikh faith alone does not establish the required interest in an institution maintained for a distinct religious sect whose beliefs and practices are not Sikh.
material_facts: The plaintiffs were Sikhs and argued that the institution was a Sikh Gurdwara, which would give them an interest in it.
The institution was registered as a branch of the principal institution of the Nirmala Sadhus, and its Mahants belonged to that order.
The evidence described the Nirmala Sadhus as followers of Vedanta and Hindu scriptural customs, and showed that the institution worshipped at a Samadhi.
The presence of the Guru Granth Sahib at the institution did not establish that it belonged to or was intended for Sikhs.
issues.conclusion: The Nirmala Sadhus could not be regarded as Sikhs, the institution was maintained for that distinct sect, and the plaintiffs’ Sikh faith did not give them sufficient interest to institute the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires an interest in the particular trust, not merely a general religious affiliation. In determining whether the institution was Sikh, the Court considered the beliefs and practices of the Nirmala Sadhus and relied on Hem Singh v. Basant Das and Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee v. Ram Parshad concerning the distinct status of ascetic sects that venerate Samadhis and retain Hindu practices. The Court also referred to Bawa Ishar Das v. Dr. Mohan Singh on the insufficiency of reading Sikh scriptures at a sectarian institution to make it a Sikh Gurdwara.

rule.if: public_trust_administration_suit and claimant_is_sikh and institution_managed_by_nirmala_order and nirmala_followers_adopt_vedanta_and_hindu_customs and institution_worships_at_samadhs

predicates.public_trust_administration_suit: The proceeding seeks relief concerning the administration of a public trust.
predicates.claimant_is_sikh: The claimant follows the Sikh faith.
predicates.institution_managed_by_nirmala_order: The institution is maintained by members of the Nirmala order.
predicates.nirmala_followers_adopt_vedanta_and_hind: The members of the order follow Vedanta and adopt Hindu scriptural customs.
predicates.institution_worships_at_samadhs: Worship at the institution is directed to a Samadhi.
predicates.sikh_identity_alone_does_not_establish_s: The claimant’s Sikh faith alone does not give the claimant sufficient interest in the institution to bring the administration suit.

issues.definition: When a Sikh claimant brings an administration suit concerning an institution maintained by an order whose members follow Vedanta and Hindu customs and worship at Samadhis, the claimant’s Sikh faith alone does not establish sufficient interest.
